Question: Penni Precisely buys \(\$ 100\) worth of stock in each of three companies: Alabama Almonds, Boston Beans, and California Cauliflower. After one year, AA was up \(20 \%,\) BB was down \(25 \%,\) and CC was unchanged. For the second year, AA was down \(20 \%\) from the previous year, BB was up \(25 \%\) from the previous year, and CC was unchanged. If \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are the final values of the stock, then
Solution:
Each second-year percentage applies to the value after the first year, so calculate the two years in order.

AA first gains \(20\%\) of \(100\), reaching \(120\) dollars. It then loses \(20\%\) of \(120\), which is \(24\) dollars. Thus
\[
A=120-24=96.
\]
BB first loses \(25\%\) of \(100\), leaving \(75\) dollars. It then gains \(25\%\) of \(75\), which is \(18.75\) dollars. Thus
\[
B=75+18.75=93.75.
\]
CC remains unchanged throughout, so \(C=100\).

Since \(93.75<96<100\), the final values satisfy \(B<A<C\), choice E.
